note: Final rules: MeitY notification G.S.R. 846(E), New Delhi, 13 November 2025 (Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Sec. 3(i)). Commencement per rule 1: rules 1, 2, 17-21 on publication; rule 4 one year after; rules 3, 5-16, 22, 23 eighteen months after. Dates computed from 13 Nov 2025. Corrigendum G.S.R. 892(E) not yet reviewed. Summaries are paraphrases, not legal text.

provisions.title: Short title and commencement
provisions.summary: Staggered commencement: rules 1, 2, 17-21 on publication; rule 4 after one year; rules 3, 5-16, 22, 23 after eighteen months.

provisions.title: Definitions
provisions.summary: Defines techno-legal measures, user account and verifiable consent (consent under rule 10 or 11).

provisions.title: Notice given by Data Fiduciary to Data Principal
provisions.summary: Notice is understandable on its own, in clear and plain language, with an itemised description of the personal data and the specified purposes, and a link and means to withdraw consent (as easily as it was given), exercise rights and complain to the Board.

provisions.title: Registration and obligations of Consent Manager
provisions.summary: Consent Managers meeting First Schedule conditions register with the Board and meet its Part B obligations.

provisions.title: Processing by the State for subsidy, benefit, service, certificate, licence or permit
provisions.summary: Such processing follows the standards in the Second Schedule.

provisions.title: Reasonable security safeguards
provisions.summary: At minimum: encryption, obfuscation, masking or tokenisation; access control; logs, monitoring and review to detect unauthorised access; continuity measures such as backups; retaining logs and personal data for one year for detection and investigation; security clauses in processor contracts; technical and organisational measures to observe safeguards. Covers processing by Data Processors too.

provisions.title: Intimation of personal data breach
provisions.summary: Inform each affected Data Principal without delay (description, likely consequences, mitigation, safety steps, contact). Inform the Board without delay, and within 72 hours (or longer if the Board allows on written request) give detailed information, facts and reasons, mitigation, findings on who caused it, remedial measures and a report of intimations to Data Principals.

provisions.title: Time period for specified purpose to be deemed as no longer being served
provisions.summary: Data Fiduciaries in Third Schedule classes erase personal data after the specified period of inactivity unless law requires retention; inform the Data Principal at least 48 hours before erasure; retain personal data, traffic data and processing logs for at least one year (including at Data Processors) for Seventh Schedule purposes.

provisions.title: Contact information of person to answer questions about processing
provisions.summary: Prominently publish, and include in every rights response, business contact information of the DPO (if applicable) or a person who can answer processing questions.

provisions.title: Verifiable consent for processing of personal data of child
provisions.summary: Obtain verifiable consent of the parent before processing a child's data, with due diligence that the parent is an identifiable adult, using reliable identity/age details held or provided (including via a virtual token from an authorised entity).

provisions.title: Verifiable consent for person with disability who has lawful guardian
provisions.summary: Verify that the guardian giving consent was appointed by a court, designated authority or local level committee under guardianship law.

provisions.title: Exemptions from certain obligations for processing of personal data of child
provisions.summary: Section 9(1) and 9(3) do not apply to the classes of Data Fiduciaries and purposes in Fourth Schedule Parts A and B, subject to their conditions.

provisions.title: Additional obligations of Significant Data Fiduciary
provisions.summary: Every twelve months a DPIA and an audit, with a report of significant observations to the Board; due diligence that algorithmic software does not pose a risk to Data Principals' rights; keep personal data specified by the Central Government (and its traffic data) within India.

provisions.title: Rights of Data Principals
provisions.summary: Publish how to make rights requests and the identifiers needed; publish a grievance response period not exceeding ninety days and implement measures to meet it; allow nomination of one or more individuals.

provisions.title: Transfer of personal data outside the territory of India
provisions.summary: Personal data may be transferred abroad subject to requirements the Central Government specifies for making it available to a foreign State or entities under its control.

provisions.title: Exemption for research, archiving or statistical purposes
provisions.summary: The Act does not apply to such processing carried on in line with the Second Schedule standards.

provisions.title: Appointment of Chairperson and other Members
provisions.summary: Search-cum-Selection Committees recommend Board Chairperson and Members.

provisions.title: Salary, allowances and conditions of service of Chairperson and Members
provisions.summary: As specified in the Fifth Schedule.

provisions.title: Procedure for meetings of Board and authentication of its orders
provisions.summary: How the Board meets and authenticates orders, directions and instruments.

provisions.title: Functioning of Board as digital office
provisions.summary: The Board works as a digital office using techno-legal measures.

provisions.title: Terms and conditions of officers and employees of Board
provisions.summary: As specified in the Sixth Schedule.

provisions.title: Appeal to Appellate Tribunal
provisions.summary: Appeals against Board orders are filed digitally with the Appellate Tribunal, with the prescribed fee.

provisions.title: Calling for information from Data Fiduciary or intermediary
provisions.summary: The Central Government may require information for Seventh Schedule purposes through authorised persons, and may bar disclosure of the request where sovereignty or security is affected.
